actions.action: Squeeze the base of the trunk monthly to check firmness
If the trunk is soft, stop watering and take the plant out of its pot
If rot is only at the base, cut off the healthy top of the cane with a sterilized saw
Let the cutting callus for 2 days, then repot it in fresh soil
Move the plant right against the brightest south- or west-facing window
Check moisture at the bottom of the pot with a long stick or moisture meter
When the soil is bone dry, drench it until water runs out of the drainage holes
Repot in a 50/50 mix of potting soil and coarse sand, pumice and perlite
Trim yellow or brown lower leaves cleanly at the base with scissors

verdict.reason: The answer blames overwatering, rot and low light rather than underwatering, and it urges the owner to withhold water, saying underwatering almost never kills, which would delay the fix this thirsty plant needed.
